samples.summary: Continue-link tests never exercise the `req.path` carry-over, the whole reason the controller builds the href from the request path
samples.evidence: `renderCliConsent(consent, req.path || '/auth/github')` (auth.controller.ts:144) exists specifically so a global path prefix or alternate router spelling is preserved instead of guessed. Every consent test goes through `consentRequest()` (spec.ts:540-549) which hard-codes `path: '/auth/github'`, so both the prefixed case (e.g. `/api/auth/github`) and the `undefined`-path fallback branch are untested — a change that hard-coded `'/auth/github'` in the controller would leave the whole suite green. Searched: the only consent tests are in the `GET /auth/github — CLI consent page` describe (spec.ts:539-626); grepped for `auth/github`/supertest across packages/backend and found no e2e coverage of this route.

samples.summary: New `continueLink` helper decodes HTML entities but no test feeds attacker-shaped values through `escapeHtml`
samples.evidence: The added helper (spec.ts:552-561) exists to un-escape the href, yet the only fixture uses `nonce: 'n0nce-x/y'` and `codeChallenge: 'c'.repeat(43)` — no `"`, `<`, `&` or `'`. The guard bounds `nonce` only by length (github-auth.guard.ts:261), so a nonce containing quotes/angle brackets is accepted and reaches `escapeHtml` (auth.controller.ts:39-46, 172-173). Deleting `escapeHtml` from the render path would not fail any test in this suite. Searched: auth.controller.spec.ts (all consent tests), github-auth.guard.spec.ts, and grepped for `escapeHtml` usages/tests.

samples.summary: Framing/caching header test asserts only that the mocked `res.set` was called; nothing pins the headers to an actual response, nor their absence elsewhere
samples.evidence: `expect(res.set).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expect.objectContaining({...}))` (spec.ts:612-618) checks a jest mock on a fully synthetic Response. It is meaningful for the values, but the assertion cannot detect ordering/emission problems (e.g. headers set after the body is flushed by a real Express response), and there is no complementary test that a normal (non-consent) start does not emit these. Acceptable for a unit suite, noted as the outer bound of what this coverage proves.

searchedFor: read github-auth.guard.spec.ts (confirmedContext/cliQuery build the query literally)
finding.summary: CLI consent page test never asserts that the continue link carries `nonce` and `code_challenge`
finding.evidence: `renders the interstitial instead of starting the login` only asserts the HTML contains `http://127.0.0.1:9876`, `cli_confirm=tok-123` and `/auth/github?mode=cli&port=9876`. `renderCliConsent` also puts `nonce` and `code_challenge` on the href, and the guard hard-refuses a resumed start missing either (`BadRequestException('Missing or invalid nonce' / 'code_challenge')`, github-auth.guard.ts). If either parameter were dropped from the link, every CLI login would 400 after the consent click and the entire suite would stay green — no other test drives the render→click round trip (grep for `nonce` in auth.controller.spec.ts only hits the callback tests; github-auth.guard.spec.ts builds its confirmed query by hand rather than from the rendered page).

verdict.reason: The claimed missing assertion exists in the same file and same describe block. `packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.spec.ts:589-601` ("carries every binding the guard requires on the continue link") renders the real consent page via `renderConsent` (spec:563-571, which invokes the unmocked `controller.githubAuth` -> `renderCliConsent`), extracts and unescapes the Continue link's href with the `continueLink` helper (spec:552-561), and asserts `Object.fromEntries(link.searchParams)` with `toEqual` against the full expected query including `nonce: 'n0nce-x/y'` and `code_challenge: 'c'.repeat(43)` (spec:597-598), plus `link.pathname === '/auth/github'`. Dropping either parameter from `renderCliConsent`'s URLSearchParams (auth.controller.ts:165-171, rendered into the href at auth.controller.ts:172,204) fails this test, so the "entire suite would stay green" premise is false. The regex `/href="([^"]+)"/` reliably matches the Continue anchor because the rendered document's head uses an inline <style> block with no other href (auth.controller.ts:175-204). The finding's evidence that grep for `nonce` in this spec only hits callback tests is incorrect — it hits spec:545 and spec:597 inside the consent block.
